surprises: THE BIG ONE: 69% of this category is a single wholesale customer, not the 5,000 residents. Rs 8,79,331 of the Rs 12,68,279 core pulse value (12m to 2026-08-21) is billed out of the 'Basement' warehouse to customer 002CM 'Hunger Heroes' across just 5 bills. Resident retail through Ary Pos is Rs 3,88,164 over 6,399 bill lines — about Rs 6.5 per resident per month on dal, in a store doing Rs 1,493 per resident per month.

The loose 'weigh-and-pack' counter everyone would recommend already exists — but it is 2 months old and it is not retail. The whole '_L' range (Chana White_L, Rajma_L, Kala Chana_L, Mah Dhuli_L, Moong Sabat_L, Moong Dhuli_L, Channa Dal_L, Arhar Dal_L, Lobia_L, Mix Dal_L, Masari Dal_L, Besan_L, plus Atta_L, Rice_L, Sugar_L, Tea_L, 20 spice rows) first billed 2026-06-23 and replaced an identical 1-kg-pouch institutional list that ran 2025-09-15 to 2026-05-11. Same warehouse, same customer. No resident has ever bought loose dal from it.

The 13 SKUs actually named 'Loose …' (Loose Arhar Daal, Loose Mung Daal, Loose Rajma Chitra, Loose Lobia, Loose Urad Sabat, Raja Loose Chana Daal / Kabuli Chana / Masoor Malka / Black Chana / Rajma Chitra / Mung Daal, Metro Loose Chana Daal…) sold ZERO units in 12 months. The old retail loose channel is dead on the books.

Retail pulses are 100% 500 g pouches. Every single one of the 30 pulse SKUs that sold at Ary Pos is a 500 g pack (bar one 1 kg besan). All 17 '250 Gm' SKUs in group 142 sold zero, and no 1 kg pulse pack sold at retail at all — the 1 kg rows only move on the institutional bill. There is no small (200-250 g) pack the market will actually buy, which is exactly the format staff families with babies need.

57% of the aisle is dead catalogue: 128 active core pulse SKUs, only 55 sold anything in 12 months. Much of the dead half is duplicate rows with SAP-ish suffixes — 'Raja Urad Sabat 500 Gm 3768 / 3770 / 3773', 'Raja Masoor Malka 250 Gm 3740 / 3741 / 3745', 'Kabuli Chana 500 Gm 277 / 300'.

Margins are near zero on the institutional line. PurchaseDetail vs SaleDetail on the same 12m: Chana White_L in at Rs 113.5/kg, out at Rs 115.0/kg (1.3%); Kabuli Chana 1 Kg in at Rs 110, out at Rs 113 (2.7%); Besan_L 1.7%. Purchases mirror sales 1:1 in the same pack — no sack-breaking, no own-packing, so none of the 15-30% loose margin the category is supposed to earn is being captured.

Amul Organic is the ONLY organic pulse brand carried — 6 SKUs (chana dal, chitra rajma, kabuli, whole moong, whole urad, red rajma) — and every one of them sold zero units in 12 months. Any organic push here would be a second attempt, not a first.

Group 142 'Pulses' alone misses about a third of the aisle's value because of misfiling: Kala Chana_L sits in Atta & Other Flours > Flours; Lobia_L / Mix Dal_L / Masari Dal_L sit in Veg Delight > Daal; Raja Dry Matar 500 Gm sits in Pulses > Chana; Raja Mung Dal/Sabat and Mixed Daal 1 Kg and Raja Kulath Daal sit in Rice & Other Grains > 'Pulses & Lenitils' (a subgroup that also holds Jivo chia/flax/pumpkin seeds and sliced black olives). The 5 'Gtc' 500 g SKUs (arhar, black chana, chana daal, urad sabat) are ALL filed under subgroup 'Arhar' regardless of contents.

No pulse SKU is sold at Ary Lite, either canteen, Ary Clothing or the Fruits & Vegetables counter — the entire category runs through Ary Pos and Basement only. The Rs 5-20 impulse formats a residential-school population actually buys (Haldiram Moong Daal 40 Gm at 2,207 packs, Haldiram Salted Peanut 40 Gm at 2,106, Haldiram Roasted Crush Peanuts 38Gm at 2,319) sit in Confectionery and never reach the Lite counter.

Two lines the ideal list under-rated are already proven here: Kulth (pahari horse gram) sells 112 packs a year as Raja Kulath Daal 500 Gm despite being rated only nice-to-have, and roasted gram is the single largest SKU in the whole category (Sunil Roasted Gram 200 Gm, 2,384 packs / Rs 83,440) — bigger than any actual dal.

Chilka is completely absent. Zero rows in 21,466 SKUs match chilka/chhilka in any spelling, so ARY has no urad chilka and no moong chilka. That is not just two missing SKUs — it makes the maa-chole di dal langar blend impossible to assemble in-house, in a Kalgidhar Trust township where that is the dish the whole campus eats.

Data window caveat: the sales/purchase feeds stop at 2026-08-21 14:05 (the internal physical stock audit noted in ary doctor / schema-notes), so the 12-month window used throughout is 2025-08-22 to 2026-08-21 and is gross of returns — SaleHeader has no cancellation flag, only separate SaleReturn documents. Total ARY sales in the same window were Rs 7.71 Cr, so pulses (broad, incl. besan, soya, roasted gram, dal namkeen, papad, peanuts = Rs 17.79 L) are 2.3% of the store; core dry pulses + besan alone are 1.6%.
